tabachnikov-example.alt: A coherent convex octagon realizing the curvatures $(3,1.2,2.2,0.8,2.6,1,1.6,0.7)$, and its eight circles through consecutive vertex triples, whose centers lie inside the vertex angles. Computed numerically and checked to double precision.
tabachnikov-example.label: fig:example

tabachnikov-method.alt: The method, computed for the word $\mu=(1,\allowbreak\,0.94,\allowbreak\,0.63,\allowbreak\,0.44,\allowbreak\,1.75,\allowbreak\,1.88,\allowbreak\,1.25,\allowbreak\,0.56,\allowbreak\,0.5)$. (a) The frame of four active edges $e_0,\dots,e_3$ (shaded) and their eight endpoint readings (black); the other readings (grey) are dormant. (b) A regular anchor: the dormant edges have length zero, each block of vertices between two active edges is a single point (open circles), and the polygon is a quadrilateral. (c) The implicit function theorem opens the dormant edges to small positive lengths, keeping every prescribed curvature. (d) Another realization of the same word, for comparison.
tabachnikov-method.label: fig:method

tabachnikov-anchor.alt: The regular anchor of \ref{fig:method}(b). Only the four active edges have positive length; the blocks $\{1,2,3\}$ and $\{5,\dots,8\}$ have collapsed to points (open circles). On active edge $e_j$ the two arcs have curvatures $s_j$ (blue) and $f_j$ (orange), the readings at its two ends. The turn at each corner is the sum of the two chord angles of the arcs meeting there, as in~\eqref{eq:controller}.
tabachnikov-anchor.label: fig:anchor

tabachnikov-construct-R.alt: Construction (R) for $\mu=(1,\allowbreak\,0.57,\allowbreak\,0.70,\allowbreak\,0.83,\allowbreak\,1,\allowbreak\,0.52,\allowbreak\,0.70,\allowbreak\,0.87)$, whose maximum $1$ is attained at $0$ and $J=4$. The frame is $(0,J-1,J,n-1)$ and the anchor is an orthogonal quadrilateral (dashed diagonals; \ref{lem:core}). Dormant readings are grey; the arcs are as in \ref{fig:anchor}. Bottom row: the anchor, the polygon after opening the dormant edges, and a zoom on the block $\{1,2,3\}$, which is a single point in the anchor and now has short dormant edges (orange).
tabachnikov-construct-R.label: fig:R

tabachnikov-construct-F.alt: Construction (F) for $\mu=(1,\allowbreak\,0.96,\allowbreak\,0.87,\allowbreak\,0.78,\allowbreak\,1.26,\allowbreak\,1.30,\allowbreak\,0.89,\allowbreak\,0.48)$, with maximum at $H=5$. The frame $(0,i-1,i,n-1)$ sits at the first transition $i=4$ on the rising leg towards $H$. Here $t=\mu_3\le p=\mu_1$, so the anchor comes from the chart used when $pt<1$ and is not orthogonal. Bottom row: the anchor, the polygon after opening the dormant edges, and a zoom on the block $\{1,2,3\}$, which is a single point in the anchor and now has short dormant edges (orange).
tabachnikov-construct-F.label: fig:F

tabachnikov-construct-N.alt: Construction (N) for $\mu=(1,\allowbreak\,0.96,\allowbreak\,0.81,\allowbreak\,0.67,\allowbreak\,1.04,\allowbreak\,0.75,\allowbreak\,0.83,\allowbreak\,0.92)$: the secondary peak is $0$ and the maximum is $H=4$, and both flags are negative. The frame is $(0,H-1,H,n-1)$ and the anchor is an orthogonal quadrilateral (dashed diagonals; \ref{lem:core}). Bottom row: the anchor, the polygon after opening the dormant edges, and a zoom on the block $\{1,2,3\}$, which is a single point in the anchor and now has short dormant edges (orange).
tabachnikov-construct-N.label: fig:N

tabachnikov-hexagon.alt: Left: the levels of strict four-vertex windows of $\kappa^s$. Right: realizing hexagons at $s=0$ and $s=1$ with their smallest enclosing circles. The reciprocal enclosing radius is at most $7$ at $s=0$, at least $11$ at $s=1$, and never $9$, so it cannot vary continuously.
tabachnikov-hexagon.label: fig:hexagon

tabachnikov-side-tangent-circle.alt: The selected circle is tangent to three supporting lines, with its central contact in the open edge. Here one neighbouring contact lies beyond its edge. All coordinates, circle equations and contact parameters in this example are checked with exact rational arithmetic.
tabachnikov-side-tangent-circle.label: fig:side-tangent-circle

tabachnikov-side-tangent-construction.alt: A balanced polygon circumscribed about the unit circle (left) and its positive edge scaling (right). The prescribed cyclic radii are $(1,2,1,3/2,1,2,1,3/2)$. Closure, strict support and all eight circles are verified exactly. The highlighted upper edge is the central edge of the circle in \ref{fig:side-tangent-circle}.
tabachnikov-side-tangent-construction.label: fig:side-tangent-construction
